body: {"total":7,"records":[{"title":"Remote blood pressure monitoring after hypertensive pregnancy: a pragmatic trial in two maternity units","authors":"Nkemelu-Forsberg A, Castellano-Hart D, Iwu-Lindqvist P","year":2021,"venue":"Orrinford Journal of Maternal Medicine","doi":"10.5555/ojmm.2021.0233","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We allocated 440 women discharged after a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy to remote blood pressure monitoring with text-message reporting or to usual community checks. Blood pressure was recorded between days 3 and 10 in 92 percent of women with remote monitoring and 44 percent with usual care. Readmission for hypertension within six weeks was 3.1 percent with remote monitoring and 4.0 percent with usual care, a difference the trial was not powered to detect. Women in the remote arm more often had their medicines reduced before six weeks. Most women found remote monitoring reassuring. The trial excluded women without a smartphone."},{"title":"Timing of peak blood pressure after pre-eclampsia and gestational hypertension","authors":"Varga-Oyelowo S, Holm-Achebe J","year":2017,"venue":"Harthill Obstetric Medicine Letters","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We reviewed twice-daily blood pressure readings for 356 women with pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension during the first two weeks after birth, from inpatient charts and home readings. Blood pressure peaked between days 3 and 6 after birth in 71 percent of women, often after discharge. Women with pre-eclampsia and those who had stopped antihypertensive medicine before discharge had the highest peaks. Severe readings of 160 over 110 or more occurred in 14 percent of women, most at home. Home readings were taken on devices of different makes, and some women stopped recording after the first week."},{"title":"Self-management of postpartum hypertension with home monitoring and medication titration: blood pressure at six weeks","authors":"Lindgren-Obi K, Marsh-Takahashi R","year":2023,"venue":"Vellmar Women's Health Reports","doi":"10.5555/vwhr.2023.0118","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"Women with postpartum hypertension were allocated to self-management, with home monitoring and medication titration by a written protocol, or to usual care. Mean diastolic blood pressure at six weeks was 5 mmHg lower with self-management, and blood pressure below 140 over 90 at six weeks was reached by 76 percent of women with self-management and 61 percent with usual care. Fewer women in the self-management group were still taking antihypertensive medicine at six weeks. The trial was small and conducted in one hospital, and women who agreed to take part were more often educated beyond school."},{"title":"Readmission for postpartum hypertension: incidence and predictors in a regional population","authors":"Petrakis-Mensah L, Ferreira-Doyle N","year":2019,"venue":"Orrinford Journal of Maternal Medicine","doi":"10.5555/ojmm.2019.0087","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"Using regional hospital records for 9,820 women with a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, we examined readmission for hypertension within six weeks of birth. Readmission occurred in 7 percent of women and was more common after pre-eclampsia, in women aged over 35 and in women discharged without antihypertensive medicine despite high readings. Most readmissions occurred within ten days of birth. Readmitted women stayed a median of two nights. The records did not show whether blood pressure had been measured between discharge and readmission, so missed opportunities could not be counted."},{"title":"Digital exclusion in postpartum remote monitoring programmes","authors":"Adjei-Rasmussen M, Kowalski-Frost E","year":2024,"venue":"Vellmar Women's Health Reports","doi":"10.5555/vwhr.2024.0031","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We examined who took part in a postpartum remote blood pressure monitoring programme offered to all eligible women in three maternity units. Twelve percent of eligible women did not own a smartphone. Uptake of remote monitoring was 58 percent among women who needed an interpreter and 86 percent among other women. Offering a loan phone and a paper diary with phone calls from the hub raised uptake among women without a smartphone to 71 percent. Women living in the most deprived areas submitted readings on fewer days. Programmes that rely on a smartphone app alone risk widening inequalities in postpartum care."},{"title":"Women's experiences of measuring their own blood pressure with a newborn at home","authors":"Olawale-Brennan T, Sato-Lund F","year":2020,"venue":"Harthill Obstetric Medicine Letters","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We held semi-structured conversations with 22 women who monitored their own blood pressure after a hypertensive pregnancy. Women described feeling reassured and in control, but found twice-daily readings hard to fit around feeding and broken sleep, especially in the first week. Several women said that a call from a midwife after a high reading made them feel looked after rather than alarmed. Women with other young children and those without a partner at home found monitoring hardest. Most women wanted to stop monitoring once readings were stable. Participants were recruited from one programme and were mostly fluent in English."},{"title":"Accuracy of automated home blood pressure monitors in postpartum women","authors":"Brandt-Iwu C, Mahlangu-Holt R","year":2016,"venue":"Harthill Obstetric Medicine Letters","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We compared three automated upper-arm home blood pressure monitors with observer measurements in 180 postpartum women. Two monitors met accuracy standards, with mean differences within 5 mmHg for systolic and diastolic pressure, while the third underestimated systolic pressure by about 8 mmHg at high readings. Accuracy was similar in women with and without pre-eclampsia. Correct cuff size mattered more than monitor model. We recommend using only monitors validated in pregnancy and the postpartum period and checking cuff size at the first use."}]}
